  Memory: Bodily Reenactment: When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred., Pain Recall: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event, Full Sensory Reliving: When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once

Vignette:
Kai Ahina had always been a careful man, but that didn't save him from the drunk driver who slammed into his truck on a rural highway three years ago. The impact was tremendous, and Kai's body still remembered it vividly – the crunch of metal, the shattering glass, the feeling of weightlessness as his vehicle spun out of control. When memories of that day came flooding back, Kai's body would involuntarily tense up, his arms and legs assuming the same twisted position they'd been in during the crash. His chest would ache, his head would throb, and for a moment, he was right back on that highway, reliving the terror. As a welder, Kai worked with his hands, but even the familiar smell of metal and sweat couldn't block out the occasional whiff of alcohol that would transport him back to that night. He'd be working on a project, lost in the rhythm of sparks and sizzle, when suddenly the pungent tang of booze would hit him like a punch to the gut. His mind would flash to the paramedics, cutting him free from the wreckage, the reek of liquor hanging heavy over everything. Sounds, too, could be a trigger – the screech of tires, the crunch of metal, the distant wail of sirens. Kai's wife, Nalani, had grown used to his sudden jolts of fear when they drove together, but it still worried her. "What's wrong?" she'd ask, as he gripped the door handle or slammed on the brakes. Kai couldn't explain; all he knew was that for a moment, he was back in that truck, careening out of control. Over time, these flashbacks had taken their toll. Kai found himself avoiding certain routes, dodging social gatherings where people might be drinking, and even switching to a quieter workshop on the outskirts of town, away from the din of traffic. His relationships suffered – Nalani felt like she was walking on eggshells around him, never knowing when he'd retreat into his shell again. His work, too, had begun to falter; simple tasks now required twice as much time and effort, as Kai's mind kept drifting back to that fateful night. One day, as he was working late in the shop, a car slammed on its brakes outside, and Kai felt himself reenacting the entire crash sequence – the screech of tires, the impact, the weightlessness. This time, though, something snapped inside him. He realized that he couldn't keep living like this, with his memories controlling every waking moment. The fear of losing himself entirely to these flashbacks finally propelled Kai to seek help. As he sat in the therapist's office, Kai Ahina looked worn and weary, but beneath the exhaustion lay a glimmer of determination. "I just want to be able to drive without freaking out," he said quietly. "I want to hold my wife without being haunted by...by that night." For the first time in years, Kai allowed himself to imagine a future where his memories no longer dictated every move – and with that hope came a tentative sense of possibility, like the faint glow of a welding spark igniting a new path forward.
